title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: An agent's model at step 4 uses a fact from the tool result at step 1. How does the model have access to that fact?

options.text: It keeps earlier steps in its own internal state
The program sends the earlier messages in the call
The provider stores each user's steps on its servers
It recalls the fact from its training data

items.stem: An agent's instructions and tool descriptions take 2,000 tokens and the student's question takes 100 tokens. The agent makes 4 model calls. Each call after the first also includes 500 more tokens than the previous call. How many input tokens are processed across all 4 calls?
Last week a student told the assistant they finished band-saw training, and the assistant saved that in a notes file. Today they ask to book the band saw. What should the assistant do first?

options.text: Book it, because the saved note records the training
Ask the student to repeat that the training is done
Look up the training record with a tool and follow it
Book it, then check the training record afterwards

items.stem: The assistant must still know a student's chosen project deadline after the conversation is summarized to save space, and again in that student's next session. Where should the program put it?

options.text: In the first message of the current conversation
In the summary written when the chat is compacted
In an earlier tool result left in the message list
In a notes store outside the context window

items.stem: A knowledge base of 90,000 tokens is loaded whole into the context on each of 5 model calls. Retrieval would instead add 3 chunks of 500 tokens on each call. How many fewer tokens does retrieval process across the 5 calls?
